In his statement recorded u/s 313 Cr.P.C. accused had stated that he has been falsely implicated in the present case so that complainant could get compensation and he was not even driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
He further stated that complainant himself was riding the motorcycle in a zig zag manner and the accident had taken plce due to his rashness and negligence.

11) I have heard the submissions addressed by Sh. Mukul Kumar, Ld. APP for state and Sh. Jagat Singh, Ld. Counsel for accused and carefully perused the documents on record.
12) Ld. Counsel for accused has submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove its case against the accused.
On the other hand, Ld. APP has submitted that the prosecution has successfully proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and the accused is liable to convicted.
APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE 13)

To prove the offence punishable u/s 279/338 IPC, the prosecution is required to prove the following mandatory ingredients: i) The rash or negligent act / driving which is likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person and ii) that the said rash or negligent act/ driving of the accused was the proximate cause of grievous hurt suffered by the victim.

At this stage, it is relevant to quote the following observations of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled Rathnashalvan v. State of Karnataka AIR 2007 SC 1064 :
7.

entities.text: Rathnashalvan v. State of Karnataka AIR 2007 SC 1064
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ...Culpable negligence lies in the failure to exercise reasonable and proper care and the extent of its reasonableness will always depend upon the circumstances of each case.
Rashness means doing an act with the consciousness of a risk that evil consequences will follow but with the hope that it will not.
Negligence is a breach of duty imposed by law.
In criminal cases, the amount and degree of negligence are determining factors.

A question whether the accused's conduct amounted to culpable rashness or negligence depends directly on the question as to what is the amount of care and circumspection which a prudent and reasonable man would consider it to be sufficient considering all the circumstances of the case.

Criminal rashness means hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is dangerous or wanton and the further knowledge that it may cause injury but done without any intention to cause injury or knowledge that it would probably be caused.

(underlining added)
8. As noted above, "Rashness" consists in hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is so, and that it may cause injury.
The criminality lies in such a case in running the risk of doing such an act with recklessness or indifference as to the consequences.

Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which, having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted.

sentences.text: (ii) Further, it has been stated by the complainant/victim in his examination-in-chief that the driver of the offending vehicle had taken him to the hospital where he got his treatment.
However, further perusal of record shows that the complainant/victim stated in his cross-examination that he had seen the driver for the first time in the court.
This further casts a doubt on the case of the prosecution and weakens the same as this is a material contradiction in the opinion of this court in the statement of the complainant/victim itself.
(iii) Further, the mechanical inspection report is also doubtful in the present case.

Perusal of the testimony of the mechanical inspector, who was examined as PW-2, shows that he has stated that he does not remember whether the offending vehicle was parked in the premises of the police station or not on the date of the inspection.
He also stated that he does not remember that on which side of the police station the offending vehicle was parked at the time of inspection.
He also stated that he does not remember if he drove the offending vehicle or not.
The mechanical inspector also stated that the photographs on record were not taken in his presence, and that therefore, he cannot say anything regarding authenticity of the same.
Moreover, perusal of the record shows that the offending vehicle was seized on 12th December, 2020 and mechanical inspection of the same was done on 15 December, 2020.
However, there is no explanation for this delay and for not getting the mechanical inspection done immediately after the offending vehicle was seized.
These factors further deteriorate the case of the prosecution.

Further, Head Constable Mohan, who was examined as PW-3, has stated in his cross-examination that he had not noticed any scratch marks or damage on the offending vehicle.
He also stated that there was a petrol pump situated near the spot of incident and that the investigating officer did not record statement of any public witnesses.
Further, perusal of testimony of ASI Avinesh Kumar, who was examined as PW-5, shows that he has stated that he received information regarding accident at about 12:02 AM on 5th December, 2020.
However, it is the case of the prosecution that the accident took place at around 10:30 PM on 4th December, 2020.
No explanation has been provided in regard to the above said delay of about one and a half hour for reporting the accident.
Moreover, PW-5 stated that he recorded the statement of the injured before he had prepared the rukka prior to registration of the FIR.
However, injured has stated in his cross-examination that his statement was recorded on 5 th December, 2020 in the night.
Also, PW5 also admitted in his cross-examination that he had inquired about the accident from the staff available at the petrol pump near the spot and that he had not written down their statements.
He also admitted that they have not been cited as witnesses in the present matter.
There is no explanation provided as to why these persons were not made witnesses in order to testify in the present matter.

The above contradictions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses further cast doubt on the case of the prosecution.

16) (i) It is the basic principle of criminal law that in order to hold an accused guilty of an offence, all the ingredients of that offence should be established against him beyond reasonable doubt and the burden upon accused is not so onerous and the standard expected of him is that of preponderance of probabilities.

(ii) In the case at hand, none of the ingredients was proved beyond reasonable doubt and the facts brought on record do not connect the accused with the injuries suffered by the victim and the alleged incident and thus, leaving behind a scope of reasonable and justified doubts.
The accused is certainly entitled to the benefit of the deficiencies and doubts in the case of prosecution.

Criminal rashness means hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is dangerous or wanton and the further knowledge that it may cause injury but done without any intention to cause injury or knowledge that it would probably be caused.
The criminality lies in such a case in running the risk of doing such an act with recklessness or indifference as to the consequences.
Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which, having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted.

15) (i) In the opinion of this Court, the testimony of PW-1/Complainant opens a Pandora's Box of doubts over the case of prosecution and is too weak to connect accused driver or offending vehicle to alleged offence or that he was driving the aforesaid vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
Moreover, the complainant stated in his cross-examination that he had called the police at 100 number and that he told them the make and number of the offending vehicle.
However, further perusal of record shows that the complainant/victim stated in his cross-examination that he had seen the driver for the first time in the court.
This further casts a doubt on the case of the prosecution and weakens the same as this is a material contradiction in the opinion of this court in the statement of the complainant/victim itself.
(iii) Further, the mechanical inspection report is also doubtful in the present case.
Perusal of the testimony of the mechanical inspector, who was examined as PW-2, shows that he has stated that he does not remember whether the offending vehicle was parked in the premises of the police station or not on the date of the inspection.
Moreover, perusal of the record shows that the offending vehicle was seized on 12th December, 2020 and mechanical inspection of the same was done on 15 December, 2020.
However, there is no explanation for this delay and for not getting the mechanical inspection done immediately after the offending vehicle was seized.

(iv)
Moreover, perusal of testimony of Dr. Abhijeet Singh, who had appeared on behalf of Dr. Shweta Aggarwal who had prepared the MLC, shows that he stated that the injuries mentioned in the MLC are possibly by other means like quarrel and by use of lathi and danda or by fall from stairs or roof.
The above contradictions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses further cast doubt on the case of the prosecution.
16) (i) It is the basic principle of criminal law that in order to hold an accused guilty of an offence, all the ingredients of that offence should be established against him beyond reasonable doubt and the burden upon accused is not so onerous and the standard expected of him is that of preponderance of probabilities.
(ii) In the case at hand, none of the ingredients was proved beyond reasonable doubt and the facts brought on record do not connect the accused with the injuries suffered by the victim and the alleged incident and thus, leaving behind a scope of reasonable and justified doubts.
The accused is certainly entitled to the benefit of the deficiencies and doubts in the case of prosecution.
